question: Lab-raised monkeys watched videos of monkeys recoiling in fear, edited to show either toy snakes or flowers. What did they learn?
options: To fear whichever object was on screen
To fear the snakes, but not the flowers
Nothing: fear needs a real encounter
answer: To fear the snakes, but not the flowers. The fearful behaviour on screen was identical; only the object had been spliced in. Observers came to fear toy snakes and a toy crocodile, and did not come to fear flowers or a toy rabbit. The same lesson stuck to one object and slid off the other.
move: Some lessons stick at the first telling because the learner was built for them.
trap: Assuming a watching monkey copies any fear, whatever its object.
source: Cook & Mineka, Journal of Abnormal Psychology, 1989
reference: Cook & Mineka, Observational conditioning of fear to fear-relevant versus fear-irrelevant stimuli in rhesus monkeys, Journal of Abnormal Psychology, 1989
